title: Here is an example of why cross validation of your AI results are important
author: LuckOrEdge
selftext:
If an AI generated your backtest, how do you know the code does what you think it does?

I had a gold strategy coded in NinjaTrader. I gave an AI only the rules and had it write the whole thing again in Python. Then I compared the two, trade by trade. Both had the same data and were operating on the close of the 1 minute bar.

All 72 trades, the win rate, and the biggest drawdown, to the dollar, were identical. That told me the trade logic was right.

What didn't match, and why it mattered:

* The Sharpe ratio was 19% to 24% lower in the second version. Same trades, different formula. Neither was wrong, but I'd never written down which one I used.
* My original report showed three different p values for the same setup, because the random seed wasn't fixed.
* On one group of trades the totals were $71 apart.  If a stop and the target are hit in the same 1 minute bar, which one counts first? I had never included it in the code.

None of these changed the conclusion. All of them were choices I had made without noticing, and any of them could have flattered a weaker strategy.

Make sure you always cross validate your results on an another platform and always look at a random sample of the trades visually on a chart. That way, you can see any bias of mistake done in your code. 

How do you guys cross validate the results you generated on AI?
